knowledge_point.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Linear Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u=2x+5.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot 2 \\  & =2{e}^{u} \\  & =2{e}^{2x+5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y={e}^{-3x+5}$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=-3x+5.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-3) \\  & =-3{e}^{u} \\  & =-3{e}^{-3x+5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the sum rule of differentiation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8x+{e}^{-3x+5}) \\  & =8-3{e}^{-3x+5} \\  & =-3{e}^{-3x+5}+8.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Linear Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=-4{e}^{u},\,u=2-x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-4{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =-4{e}^{u}\cdot (-1) \\  & =4{e}^{u} \\  & =4{e}^{2-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=2-ln⁡(3)$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=2-ln⁡(3)} & =4{e}^{2-(2-ln⁡(3))} \\  & =4{e}^{ln⁡(3)} \\  & =4\cdot 3 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=5{e}^{4x}$ at the point where $x=\frac{1}{4}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=5{e}^{u},\,u=4x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=5{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =5{e}^{u}\cdot 4 \\  & =20{e}^{u} \\  & =20{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=\frac{1}{4}$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=1/4} & ={(20{e}^{4x})|}_{x=1/4} \\  & =20{e}^{4(1/4)} \\  & =20e\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x={x}_{1}=\frac{1}{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={(5{e}^{4x})|}_{x=1/4} \\  & =5{e}^{4(1/4)} \\  & =5e.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-5e & =20e(x-\frac{1}{4}) \\ y-5e & =20ex-5e \\ y & =20ex\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=3{e}^{-4x-6}+6$ at the point where $x=- \frac{7}{4}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=3{e}^{u}+6,\,u=-4x-6.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=3{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =3{e}^{u}\cdot (-4) \\  & =-12{e}^{u} \\  & =-12{e}^{-4x-6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=- \frac{7}{4}$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=- \frac{7}{4}} & =-12{e}^{-4x-6}{|}_{x=- \frac{7}{4}} \\ & =-12{e}^{(-4)(- \frac{7}{4})-6} \\ & =- 12 e.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=x_1=- \frac{7}{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}y_1 & =(3{e}^{-4x-6}+6){|}_{x=- \frac{7}{4}} \\ & =3{e}^{(-4)(- \frac{7}{4})-6}+6 \\ & =6 + 3 e.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 & =m(x-x_1) \\ y-(6 + 3 e) & =(- 12 e)(x-(- \frac{7}{4})) \\ y-(6 + 3 e) & =- 12 e x-(21 e) \\ y & =- 12 e x - 18 e + 6.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=-2{e}^{-3x+2}+3$ at the point where $x=\frac{1}{3}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=-2{e}^{u}+3,\,u=-3x+2.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-2{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =-2{e}^{u}\cdot (-3) \\  & =6{e}^{u} \\  & =6{e}^{-3x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=\frac{1}{3}$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=\frac{1}{3}} & =6{e}^{-3x+2}{|}_{x=\frac{1}{3}} \\ & =6{e}^{(-3)(\frac{1}{3})+2} \\ & =6 e.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=x_1=\frac{1}{3}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}y_1 & =(-2{e}^{-3x+2}+3){|}_{x=\frac{1}{3}} \\ & =-2{e}^{(-3)(\frac{1}{3})+2}+3 \\ & =3 - 2 e.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 & =m(x-x_1) \\ y-(3 - 2 e) & =(6 e)(x-(\frac{1}{3})) \\ y-(3 - 2 e) & =6 e x-(2 e) \\ y & =6 e x - 4 e + 3.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=5{e}^{6x-4}+1$ at the point where $x=\frac{5}{6}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
y=5{e}^{u}+1,\,u=6x-4.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=5{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =5{e}^{u}\cdot 6 \\  & =30{e}^{u} \\  & =30{e}^{6x-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=\frac{5}{6}$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=\frac{5}{6}} & =30{e}^{6x-4}{|}_{x=\frac{5}{6}} \\ & =30{e}^{(6)(\frac{5}{6})-4} \\ & =30 e.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=x_1=\frac{5}{6}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}y_1 & =(5{e}^{6x-4}+1){|}_{x=\frac{5}{6}} \\ & =5{e}^{(6)(\frac{5}{6})-4}+1 \\ & =1 + 5 e.\end{aligned}

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 & =m(x-x_1) \\ y-(1 + 5 e) & =(30 e)(x-(\frac{5}{6})) \\ y-(1 + 5 e) & =30 e x-(25 e) \\ y & =30 e x - 20 e + 1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=-4{e}^{3x-5}-3$ at the point where $x=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=-4{e}^{u}-3,\,u=3x-5.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-4{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =-4{e}^{u}\cdot 3 \\  & =-12{e}^{u} \\  & =-12{e}^{3x-5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=2$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=2} & =-12{e}^{3x-5}{|}_{x=2} \\ & =-12{e}^{(3)(2)-5} \\ & =- 12 e.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=x_1=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}y_1 & =(-4{e}^{3x-5}-3){|}_{x=2} \\ & =-4{e}^{(3)(2)-5}-3 \\ & =- 4 e - 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 & =m(x-x_1) \\ y-(- 4 e - 3) & =(- 12 e)(x-(2)) \\ y-(- 4 e - 3) & =- 12 e x-(- 24 e) \\ y & =- 12 e x - 3 + 20 e.\end{aligned}
$$
